bibliography.abstract: Accurate traffic prediction is essential for urban planning but remains challenging due to the irregular patterns caused by unexpected events. While Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks (STGNNs) effectively model periodic data, they often struggle with these aperiodic fluctuations. To address this, we propose SIMBAD, which improves generalization irregular patterns via two key mechanisms: 1) adaptive regulation of periodic signals to prioritize recent signals, and 2) dynamic spatial modeling that adjusts influence between connected nodes based on contextual relations. Built upon simple similarity metrics to adapt to aperiodic patterns, SIMBAD outperforms existing methods on real-world benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance in predicting unseen and irregular traffic events.
bibliography.comment: Total of 30 pages, 9 figures (4 in main, 5 in appendix), accepted to NeurIPS(Neural Information Processing Systems) 2026
bibliography.title: SIMBAD: Spatio-Temporal Traffic Forecasting Robust to Aperiodicity

en.what: Researchers developed SIMBAD, a spatio-temporal graph neural network architecture that improves traffic forecasting during unexpected, irregular events. The model combines adaptive temporal regulation to prioritize recent conditions over historical rhythms with dynamic spatial modeling that reweights node connections based on contextual similarity. Evaluation on real-world benchmark datasets shows SIMBAD outperforms existing traffic prediction methods when handling unseen, aperiodic patterns.
en.why: Standard spatio-temporal models degrade during unscheduled incidents because they rely heavily on historical periodicity; SIMBAD provides a mechanism to maintain predictive accuracy when traffic patterns deviate from routine cycles.
